title: Spicy pani puri from scratch 🌿💦 #shorts
dish_fact: Pani puri goes by a different name in almost every Indian city - golgappa in Delhi, puchka in Kolkata, gup chup in the east - but the shatter-crisp shell and the cold spiced water are loved everywhere.

segments.moment_description: Bright village kitchen garden morning: the young woman gathers a big handful of fresh mint and coriander and snaps off a green chilli, shaking the water from the leaves, dew and sunlight, Studio Ghibli style

The mint, coriander, green chilli and a knob of ginger are ground on a heavy stone sil-batta, a hand rocking the stone back and forth until it becomes a glossy, vivid green paste, close-up of the fragrant crush

The green paste is whisked into a big bowl of cold water with a spoon of tamarind pulp, black salt, roasted cumin and chaat masala; the water swirls into a cloudy spicy-green pani, then a few ice cubes are dropped in with a splash
In a separate bowl, boiled potato cubes and soft chickpeas are mashed roughly and tossed with black salt and chaat masala into a spiced filling, a tight close-up of the spoon folding it together
A thumb cracks a neat hole in the top of a crisp round puri shell and tucks in a spoon of the potato-chickpea masala, the shell shattering slightly at the edges, macro shot
The filled puri is dunked deep into the green pani, lifted out dripping and overflowing, and set onto a leaf plate lined with more ready puris - the mouthwatering reveal, cold droplets falling
